Bench: P.Sree Sudha
The Honourable Smt. Justice P.Sree Sudha
 M.A.C.M.A.No.3213 of 2008
J U D G M E N T:

This Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act,
1988 against the Judgment and Decree dated 07.12.2006 passed in O.P.No.248 of 2004 passed by the learned Chairman, Motor Vehicles Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional District Judge,
Mahabubnagar.

entities.text:
Motor Vehicles Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional District Judge,
Mahabubnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 02. The appellant/petitioner filed O.P.No.248 of 2004, claiming compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- for injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 16.09.2003.
The trial Court after considering the arguments of both sides, granted compensation of Rs.25,000/-.
Aggrieved by the said Judgment, petitioner therein preferred the present appeal.
There is no dispute regarding the accident, but the quantum of the compensation is only disputed, this Court is no going into other details.
03. The petitioner himself was examined as PW1.

He also got examined Doctor as PW2 who issued Ex.A5 disability certificate opining that the petitioner got 35% disability and he cannot attend hard labour like lifting weights and that the petitioner suffers from diffuse brain injury and vision of left eye of petitioner also diminishes, as a consequence of road traffic accident and he found on diagnosis of left hand and leg that the disability is permanent in nature and the petitioner needs prolonged medication of physiotherapy.
04. PW1 stated that he was referred to Osmania General Hospital and he was treated from 27.09.2003 to 07.10.2003 as inpatient.
He also undergone treatment at Area Hospital, Narayanapet on 16.09.2003.
Ex.A6 is the case sheet which show that the petitioner sustained several injuries including head injury.
Though disability certificate shows 35% of disability, it was not believed by the trial Court on the ground that the disability certificate was not issued by the Medical Board.
05. The petitioner is a mason by profession and earning Rs.4,000/- per month as per record.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, as such it is reasonable to award Rs.25,000/- for injuries.

Apart from that he is also entitled for an amount of Rs.15,000/- for pain and suffering and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of amenities and he is also entitled for Rs.10,000/-
towards medical expenses, Rs.5,000/- towards transportation charges and Rs.5,000/- towards extra nourishment.

The petitioner might not have attended his work, atleast for a period of six months,
therefore, he is also entitled for an amount of Rs.24,000/- towards loss of earnings.

1 06.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, the appellant/petitioner is entitled for the compensation in the following terms:
1. Injuries Rs.25,000/-
2. Pain and Suffering Rs.15,000/-
3. Loss of Amenities Rs.15,000/-
4. Medical Expenses Rs.10,000/-
5. Transportation Charges Rs.5,000/-
6. Extra nourishment Rs.5,000/-
7. Loss of earnings Rs.24,000/-
 TOTAL Rs.99,000/-
 07.

In the result, the Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount from Rs.25,000/- to Rs.99,000/-
(Rupees Ninety Nine Thousand only) with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing the petition till date of realization.

Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount and Respondent No.2/Insurance Company shall deposit the entire amount within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this Judgment.
On such deposit, the appellant is entitled to withdraw the said amount along with interest accrued thereon.
There shall be no order as to costs.

Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
